pr.title: Number inbox items from 1 in each session
pr.head: 0efb6f641d8c1ce8ab8f11d6150f768024d5216c

summary: Projector's inbox holds the questions and notices an agent posts for you. An agent posts one with the ask or tell tool, or with project inbox ask and project inbox tell. Claude Code's band, the strip above your prompt, lists the items, and an answer goes back to the agent as a line that starts ANSWER or DISMISSED. Each session keeps its items as JSON files in its own directory under Projector's state directory.

Before this change, an item's reference, the handle the CLI prints and takes, named its pull request: #337.3 was the session's third item about #337, octo/web#12.1 the first about another repository's #12, and q2 the second about no pull request. The forms existed so you could type one in a prompt, but nobody does: the band shows no reference, and you answer by pressing in the band. The forms still cost a count per pull request, a recorded session repository, a git call on every post, and a project inbox context process for any prompt that looked like it held a reference.

Now each session numbers its items 1, 2, 3 in one count across questions and notices, kept in count.json. The reference is that number as a string. The agent reads it in what the tools return and in the ANSWER lines, and a shell user reads it in project inbox list. You never see it: the band, the notifications, and the failed-delivery toast name an item by its subject.

This builds section 11 of the inbox plan, which #294 added. Nothing migrates: an item stored under an old reference is never read again, and every command refuses the old forms with exit 65. Because every session counts from 1, a number typed in a shell with no session named looks first among open items, so it finds the one session that holds it open rather than every session's resolved item of the same number.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Item: a question, which you answer or dismiss, or a notice, which you read and dismiss.
  • Reference: the item's handle, stored as ref. Now its number as a string, such as "3"; an answer adds a letter, as 3.a.
  • Session: one agent conversation; each has its own store directory and its own count.
  • The band: Projector's Claude Code plugin view above the prompt, which lists the session's items by running project inbox list --json.
  • Deliverer: whatever sends an answer back to the agent, the band or project inbox watch.

cards.title: What goes away
cards.html:
• project inbox context, which now exits 2 as an unknown subcommand.
  • The band's reading of references in a sent prompt: mayReference and explain.
  • counts.json, session.json, session_repo, checkout_repo, and the repo argument of post.
  • The stdin argument of the band's project helper, which only explain used.

groups.title: The store and the CLI
groups.kicker: How a session numbers its items, and how the CLI names them
intro: The Python side owns the store. post, which records every item, now takes the session's lock, reads last from count.json, writes last + 1 back, and then writes the item to <number>.json. The count is written first, so a crash between the two writes skips a number rather than handing it out twice. The count only grows, so pruning, which deletes the oldest delivered items, can never free a number for reuse.

Two checks keep the old forms out. REFERENCE, the pattern every command parses its argument with, now accepts only a number with an optional letter. item_in, the check that decides whether a file holds an item, now also requires a whole-number ref, so a file written under #337.3 or q2 is skipped by every reader.

Every session keeps up to 100 resolved items, and its directory stays after it ends, so most sessions hold a 1. To keep a bare answer 3.a from a shell useful, locate, which finds the session holding a number when none is named, now takes prefer_open. With it, the candidates are the sessions whose item has no answer recorded, whenever any does; otherwise every session that holds the number, as before. show, answer, dismiss, and snooze pass it.

checks.text: A number open in two sessions still exits 67, and the message says to pass the session that list prints beside the item. --session or PROJECTOR_SESSION skips the lookup entirely, and the band and watch always pass a session.

groups.title: The band and the tools
groups.kicker: What the Claude Code plugin returns, shows, and stops reading
intro: The band is the TypeScript plugin in hooks/. Its ask and tell tools run the CLI and return what it prints, so they now answer Asked 3. and Posted 3., and the tool description gives 3 as its example.

Three things you see change. A tool's notification now holds the subject alone. The toast for an answer that did not reach its agent quotes the question's subject in place of its reference. And the prompt.submit hook, which ran when you sent a prompt, no longer looks for references in it or runs project inbox context; it still adds the note that names a subagent whose question your prompt answers.

checks.text: The band reads only its own session's store, so keying items, drawers, and deliveries by ref stays unambiguous now that every session counts from 1. Traced readStore and its one caller, which passes $.session.id().

The band actions main added run project inbox with --session, like every other band call, so the lookup that prefers open items never applies to the band. Checked every ['inbox', …] call in register.tsx; claude plugin test . passed 78 of 78.

checks.text: This lookup runs after replace has stored the reopened item, so the question is normally in the list; when it is not, the toast says "an answer" and still names no number. The band test for a dropped submit expects the quoted subject, and claude plugin test . passed 78 of 78.

An older band paired with this CLI still runs project inbox context on a prompt shaped like an old reference. The CLI now exits 2 there, and the older explain already treats any failure as no added context.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: The CLI and band docs, and what building the plan settled
intro: The CLI guide and the band guide now use numbers in every example, and drop the reference forms, the session repository, and project inbox context. The CLI guide also says how a bare number is looked up. The inbox plan gains section 11.10, which records the points building section 11 settled, such as the toast's wording when it cannot find the question and why a bare number prefers open items. The plan stays in-progress until a check by hand under tmux.
